coordinateConventions.columns: 0-based UTF-16 CODE UNITS, as on the wire and as measured by String.prototype.length
lineTable: Layer 1 §2.1: the line table splits on U+000A (LF) ONLY and RETAINS any preceding
U+000D (CR) inside the line's text. A text ending in LF therefore has a final, empty
line, and an LF itself occupies NO column. A column equal to the line's length is
in-bounds and denotes end-of-line. V6 depends on all three of these facts.
warning: A UTF-16 code-unit column is not a Unicode code-point index and not a UTF-8
byte offset. Vector V5 pins all three apart deliberately: for the same
position they are 11, 10, and 13 respectively. An implementation that counts
code points (the natural error in Python-like languages) or bytes (the
natural error in Rust) fails V5 and only V5.

The rules that do the most work, and the vectors that pin them:
§2.3  resolveAt is LINE-SCOPED and is NOT sourceless-transparent          V2, V7
§2.6  the emission standard: exactly five kinds of segment are emitted    all
§5.3(a) resume segment at a replaced range's end; carried input segments  V1, V2, V9
§5.3(b) a non-empty overwrite emits exactly ONE segment, at its start     V1, V10, V12
§5.3(c) an empty overwrite emits NOTHING and advances zero               V1, V2, V8
§5.3(d) end-of-walk carry, live even for empty code                       V14
§5.3  rule precedence: a replaced range drops every segment inside it     V8, V10, V12
§5.5  equal-coordinate order; the worked N-ary case                       V3, V12
§5.7  the template fragment is never rewritten                            V19
§5.8  a present fragment whose map is absent contributes NOTHING          F7, V18

§6.4  BR-3 fires iff the fragment's final code ends with LF               V13 (fires), V14 (must not, empty case), V21 (must not, ordinary non-empty case)
§7.4  stable append, NO deduplication (D-5)                               V4, V15
§7.6  canonical encoding, in sequence order, never re-sorted              V3
§7.7  requested-but-empty map vs no map at all                            V18 vs V17
TERMINAL VS NON-TERMINAL REMOVAL is the asymmetry three vectors turn on. Rule (c) emits
no segment of its own, so what FOLLOWS the removed range decides: a non-terminal removal
is followed by a surviving Original chunk whose start fires rule (a)'s resume clause,
while a terminal removal has no following chunk and therefore produces no transition
segment at all. V1 pins the terminal case, V2 and V9 the non-terminal one.
failClosedContract: Layer 1 §4.2: both fail-closed outcomes are HARD failures, and NEITHER returns a partial
result. On either outcome the assembler produces no successful result at all — not code
without a map, and not code with an empty map. Returning the assembled code while
reporting a map failure would be exactly the 'unmapped successful result' the charter
forbids. Every vector in `failClosedVectors` whose outcome is not 'composed' therefore
asserts the ABSENCE of any code and any map as well as the reported outcome; they carry
no `expected.code` for that reason, and an implementation that returns code alongside the
Validation is FAIL-FAST over a single total order (§4.1): any input for which two or more
conditions hold has ONE determined reported outcome, and the seven vectors marked ORDER
in their intent exist to pin exactly that.
annotations: Fields that are NOT part of the compared artifact, present as review aids:
`intent`, `derivation`  — prose; the derivation is the hand-working of layer 1's rules.
`inputMapsDecoded`      — a SIBLING of `input`, never inside it. The DTO carries each
fragment map as a RAW, unparsed string (§3.3 note 2), which is
required so the malformed-JSON rejections are exercisable at
all; this field restates those maps' segments in decoded form
so a reader can check them without decoding VLQ by hand.
`mapAbsentMembers`      — asserts, positively, which §7.1 members are ABSENT from the
artifact, so that an absence cannot be confused with an
omission by whoever wrote the vector.
`segments`              — the decoded segment sequence of `expected.map.mappings`, which
§7.1 compares alongside the artifact. It is redundant with
`mappings` by construction and the two must agree; a multiset
or sorted comparison of it is forbidden.
`expected.map: null` means NO MAP AT ALL and occurs only for V17, where none was
requested. It is a DIFFERENT expectation from V18's empty artifact
{ version: 3, names: [], sources: [], mappings: '' }, which is what a REQUESTED map with
zero contributing maps produces. §7.7 exists to keep those two apart.
Sub-codes are written as the dotted identifier layer 1 uses in prose throughout ('U1.9'),
not as the identifier-plus-mnemonic form its §4.4 table rows carry ('U1.9
number-outside-interoperable-domain'); the mnemonic appears in each vector's `intent`.
This is a presentation choice about how to spell §4.2's `code` field and settles no
semantics.

notesForIndependentReview: Four things a reviewer should look at directly rather than take from the derivations.
1. F45 DEPENDS ON DECISION D-8. Layer 1 §4.3's D-8 fixes U8.1's reported fragment as the
template, and F45 encodes that. D-8 is adopted (see
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/BV0A/layer1-d8-adoption.md). F45 is the ONLY vector
affected; if D-8 were ever revised by a further amendment, its `fragment` changes and
nothing else in this file does.
2. A SOURCE-BEARING RESUME SEGMENT AFTER A REMOVAL IS UNREACHABLE, and V9 covers the
reachable neighbour instead. A removal's pattern ends with the LF it consumes, so the
offset just past the match is always column 0 of a line; a source-bearing lookup there
requires a segment AT column 0, which makes seg(o) non-empty and SUPPRESSES the resume
segment in favour of the carried one (§5.3(a) and its payload-precedence rule). So the
two reachable outcomes at a removal's old end are a sourceless resume segment (V2) or a
carried source-bearing segment with the resume suppressed (V9). A rule-(a) resume
segment carrying a source-bearing payload IS reachable after a non-empty overwrite,
where the old end falls mid-line, and V1, V5 and V6 pin that. This is an observation
about what the frozen algebra makes reachable, not a gap in it.
3. F7's SYNTHETIC SCRIPT BYTES ARE MODELLED, NOT SPECIFIED. Layer 1 §6.4 says the real
block is non-empty and contains `const __sfc__` and `export default __sfc__`, and
fixes no more than that. F7 and V18 use a shape carrying both constructs. Their
OUTCOMES do not depend on the spelling — only on the fragment being present, not
authored, and map-less — but their `expected.code` does, so if the real block's bytes
are ever pinned, those two code strings are what to re-check.
4. EVERY VECTOR IS NOW AN ASSEMBLY-LEVEL VECTOR. Revision 1's V1-V3 and V5-V7 were
chain-level: their `expected.code` was the post-rewrite FRAGMENT code, carrying none
of §6.2's assembly writes, which is why layer 1 §9's table records BR-3 as outside
what they assert. Binding `input` to the §3.3 AssembleInput schema makes that reading
unavailable — the DTO is the ASSEMBLER's input and has exactly one defined output — so
each now states the whole module and gains its BR-3 segment. Their DTOs are chosen to
keep the scaffolding minimal (no styles, no custom blocks, no template, production, no
HMR), so the script's placement is (0,0) and every chain coordinate revision 1 asserted
is UNCHANGED. V16 is the vector that deliberately does the opposite.

derivation: PASS 1 is V1's for lines 0 and 1. Line 2 'const tail = 1' contains no occurrence,
so its single input segment is carried unchanged at (2,6).
line 0 is 20 units, line 1 is 25, line 2 is 14, each LF-terminated.
PASS 2. The removal target occupies [21,47) and text continues to 62, so a
following Original[47,62) EXISTS and rule (a)'s first clause fires a resume
segment at offset 47. The empty overwrite advanced the generated position by
zero, so that segment lands at generated (1,0).
ITS PAYLOAD IS SOURCELESS, and this is the whole point of the vector. lookup(47)
is resolveAt at pass-1 coordinate (2,0). The ONLY segment on line 2 is at column
6, which is AFTER column 0, so no segment on that line is applicable and the

This vector fails an implementation that (a) omits the resume segment entirely,
(b) performs a global rather than line-scoped last-applicable lookup and wrongly

vectors.intent: Two segments sharing one generated coordinate keep their WIRE ORDER. A multiset or column-sorted comparator cannot distinguish this vector from its swap.
derivation: Neither rewrite pattern occurs, so both passes are the identity: a pass with no
occurrence still runs, its chunk list is the single Original[0,len) of CT-1, and
§5.3 emits every input segment at its own offset (§5.1).
Both input segments occupy generated (0,0), so they form ONE emission point, and
§5.3(a) emits EVERY segment of seg(0) in M's order. §5.5 rule 1 fixes that order.
The decoder reads the second segment's zero column delta as an ADDITIONAL segment
rather than a replacement, and resolveAt selects the LAST applicable, so a
consumer at (0,0) resolves authored (5,5), not (1,0).
Swapping the two changes that answer while leaving every multiset, every per-line
bag and every column-sorted list identical. The expected sequence — and the
expected `mappings` string, in which the swap would read 'AAKK,AAJL' — is
therefore order-significant, and this is the discriminating case for positional
comparison (§7.1 forbids a multiset or sorted comparison; §7.6 encodes in
sequence order, never re-sorted).
ASSEMBLY. Placement (0,0); the code ends with LF so BR-3 fires at module line 1,
where W-18's bytes are written.

vectors.intent: Source and name tables are a STABLE APPEND with NO deduplication (§7.4 DECISION D-5) even when both fragments declare identical spellings; template indices are remapped by the append offset; and placement is DERIVED from the write grammar. Corrected here to the COMPLETE five-segment result layer 1 §9.1 spells out — the seed's three-segment expectation omitted both BR-3 boundary segments.
derivation: WHY THIS VECTOR CHANGED. The seed expected three segments. Layer 1 §9.1 records
that as the one genuine gap between the seed and the frozen specification: V4 is
the only seed vector that models assembly placement, so BR-3 applies to it, and
BOTH of its fragments are contributing maps whose final code ends with LF. The
correct result is FIVE segments. Layer 1 §9.1 names the two missing ones exactly
— sourceless at (1,0) from the script and at (3,0) from the template — and this
vector is now the complete assembly vector §9.1 says layer 2 must choose to make
it (the alternative it offers, re-scoping V4 to the chain level, would have
discarded its placement coverage).
TABLES (§7.4). Both fragments name the same authored file and the same authored
symbol. A deduplicating merge would emit sources ['Comp.vue'] and names ['count']
and leave both fragments' indices at 0. D-5 forbids that: two fragments'
independently declared rows are two facts that happen to be equal, not one fact
copied, and merging is itself an assertion about row identity that BV0A's opaque
carriage withholds. Under stable append the script's rows come first, then the
template's: sources ['Comp.vue','Comp.vue'], names ['count','count']. The script's
base offsets are (0,0) and the template's are (1,1), so the template's srcIdx 0
becomes 1 and its nameIdx 0 becomes 1.
SCRIPT CHAIN. The single input segment sits exactly at the overwrite start, so it
is dropped by §5.3's rule precedence and rule (b) emits one segment at the same
coordinate carrying lookup(6) — the same authored position AND the same name
index, because a rewrite never drops or renames a name binding (§5.3, 'Names').
The resume segment at generated (0,15) resolves lookup(13) to that same input
segment and carries its name index too. Pass 2 finds no occurrence and is the
identity.
PLACEMENT (§6.3), DERIVED, never supplied. The script is written by W-06 at
(0,0). Its code ends with LF, so W-07 does not fire and the cursor is at (1,0).
The template is present, so W-10 writes ONE separator LF, leaving the cursor at
(2,0) — the template's placement. Its (0,9) segment therefore lands at (2,9).
Reading the separator as absent and placing the template at line 1 is the natural
off-by-one this vector catches. The template is never rewritten (§5.7), so it has
no chain step at all.
BOUNDARY SEGMENTS (§6.4 BR-3). Both fragments are contributing maps and both end
with LF, so both fire:
script   final code 'const _sfc_main = {}\n' -> trailing empty line is fragment
line 1 -> module line 1 -> sourceless (1,0)
template final code 'function render() {}\n', placed at line 2 -> trailing empty
line is fragment line 1 -> module line 3 -> sourceless (3,0)
Each is positioned AFTER every placed segment of the fragment it bounds (§5.5
rule 6), so it wins the resolveAt tie at its own coordinate. BR-3 fires for both
unconditionally, per its own syntactic condition (§6.4 `DECISION` D-6) — it is not
evaluated against what, if anything, ends up sitting on the line it protects. Only the
TEMPLATE-side boundary protects a real assembly-owned byte: module line 3 carries
the bytes W-13' (not W-13) writes. The SCRIPT-side boundary at module line 1 protects
nothing: line 1 is
occupied only by W-10's own separator LF, and an LF occupies NO column at all (§2.1) —
this is §6.4's case 2, where the boundary fires (its syntactic predicate is met) but
there is no byte on that line for it to shadow or protect either way.
REMAINING WRITES. The template code contains 'function render(' and not
'function ssrRender(', so W-13' writes '_sfc_main.render = render\n' at (3,0);
W-18 then writes at (4,0). Neither contributes a segment (BR-1).

vectors.intent: Columns are UTF-16 CODE UNITS — not code points, and not UTF-8 bytes. This vector separates all three.
derivation: The line is 'const ' (6 units) + U+1D400 MATHEMATICAL BOLD CAPITAL A (a surrogate
PAIR, 2 UTF-16 units, 4 UTF-8 bytes) + ' = ' (3 units) + '__sfc__' (7 units).
The '__sfc__' occurrence therefore begins at:
UTF-16 code-unit column 11   <- the wire-correct value, used below (§2.1)
Unicode code-point index 10  <- what a code-point-counting language reports
UTF-8 byte offset 13         <- what a byte-counting language reports
An implementation that conflates any two of them fails this vector and no other.
§5.2 is what keeps the two spaces apart: the chunk walk runs on BYTE offsets
